method: AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS=32 (ingress cap lifted so the AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY ceiling is the binding constraint); mock pi (1.2s sleep); 8 concurrent audit_runner issue invocations per ceiling; 0.25s metric sampling.
caveat: Host baseline load was elevated (~24-43 on 16 cores) by concurrent, unrelated agent traffic, so the absolute 'load < 16' target could not be observed; the batch-attributable load delta and swap delta are the attributable signals. peak_batch_pi == ceiling confirms admission/parallelism.
conclusion: Drain time falls monotonically (18.7s -> 9.6s) as the ceiling rises 3 -> 8; batch-attributable load delta stays <= 1.63 and swap never grows. With the default ingress cap (3) peak_batch_pi saturated at 3 for every ceiling, proving AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS=3 was the binding constraint. Chosen ceilings: 6 (= 2x the 3-slot proxy pool) for both AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY and AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS - absorbs bursts while bounded proxy contention; 8 gave diminishing returns and higher fan-out.
